title: Generative models for synthetic data generation: application to pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic data

content.abstract_summary: Benchmarks PAR, TimeGAN, and MLP conditional GAN approaches on clinical-style longitudinal datasets containing covariates and PK/PD endpoints. Evaluation combines ML fidelity/usefulness scores, univariate distributional tests, and pharmacometrics-specific metrics; MLP cGAN performed best overall on most reported metrics.
key_findings: The benchmark addresses longitudinal observations, heterogeneous covariates/endpoints, and multiple treatment arms.
Evaluation included discriminative and predictive scores, Kolmogorov-Smirnov and chi-square tests, and pharmacometrics-specific measures.
MLP cGAN performed best overall for most evaluated metrics.
The work supports synthetic-data augmentation and sharing, but the accessible evidence does not establish downstream inferential equivalence, causal validity, or privacy guarantees.
limitations: Detailed full-text results were not openly accessible during extraction.
The public abstract and related PAGE study description do not provide a complete downstream model-refitting comparison.
Distributional and predictive similarity do not by themselves establish counterfactual validity or disclosure protection.

extracted_claims.text: MLP conditional GAN exhibited the best overall performance for most of the evaluated metrics.
Synthetic-data quality was evaluated using ML, univariate statistical, and pharmacometrics-related metrics.
extracted_claims.location: Abstract and associated PAGE methods summary

numerical_findings.description: Simulx-generated benchmark datasets described in the associated PAGE study

gaps_addressed: Supports M4.5-A10 and the requirement to supplement generic fidelity tests with pharmacometric and downstream model-based validation.

provenance.notes: Publication metadata and abstract verified through PubMed/EPFL. The associated PAGE abstract was used only to identify the method families and reported 12 simulated datasets; full-paper numerical extraction remains a follow-up if licensed access is available.
